author: @bitgamma

evidence.api_compatibility: Additive only — bench gains a new `PP t/s` column (TTFT/TPS columns unchanged), JSON gains optional `pp_tps` keys (existing keys preserved), comparison gains `PP change` column (shows `null` when prior run lacks prefill data). No breaking changes detected.
evidence.documentation: docs/guide/cli.md updated to describe the new `PP t/s` column, its calculation method (backend prompt-eval time when available, wall-clock TTFT as fallback), and cloud vs local backend caveats. The note about cloud models showing lower PP t/s due to routing overhead is well-written. No documentation update for the new system stats API fields (`primary_gpu_id`, `gpus`). CodeRabbit bot flagged the timing source definition as ambiguous (line 1046); the note already covers both sources but the first sentence states PP t/s as prompt_tokens/TTFT which does not match the code path that prefers `prompt_per_second` when available.
evidence.manual_release_testing: The `lemonade bench` CLI output format changes — new `PP t/s` column in table mode, `pp_tps` stats in `--json` output, `PP change` in `--compare` mode. No evidence of manual end-to-end testing on the release build.
evidence.post_approval_commits: The post-approval-commits output (after @jeremyfowers' approval at 2026-10-13T16:51:29Z) shows GPU metrics changes (nvidia_metrics.h, amd_gpu_type.h, metrics_linux.cpp, metrics_windows.cpp, server.cpp, system_info.cpp, prometheus_metrics.cpp, test additions) and a '[PATCH 20/20] mark TheNoise as Core (#3826)' commit that appear to belong to PR #3826 on the same merge queue branch (gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-3759-...). The merge commit diff itself only includes 7 prefill TPS files (bench.cpp, bench_comparison.cpp, bench_output.cpp, bench.h, bench_comparison.h, bench_output.h, cli.md). Investigate whether the merge queue branch was intended to combine multiple PRs and whether those commits were merged.
evidence.review: @iswaryaalex approved with 'Tested locally, works!' and @jeremyfowers approved with 'rubber stamp!' Neither review involved detailed code inspection. CodeRabbit bot raised two concerns — filtering zero PP values in statistics (line 77 of bench.cpp) and clarifying the PP t/s timing source definition in docs (line 1046 of cli.md) — neither was addressed by the author. Per docs/dev/contribute.md, @bitgamma (the author) and @sofiageo cover benchmarking; @bitgamma reviewed his own changes. @jeremyfowers (admin maintainer) covers new CLI commands and gave a one-word rubber-stamp approval without substantive inspection.
evidence.security: Benign — reads existing timing data from benchmark responses (`timings.prompt_per_second` or computed from `input_tokens * 1000 / ttft_ms`) and displays it. No new network calls, credential handling, code execution paths, or supply-chain changes.
evidence.tests: @iswaryaalex reports local testing. Unit tests for GpuMetricsTracker were added in test/cpp/test_system_info_helpers.cpp (89 lines) but these test GPU metrics, not the prefill TPS feature. No dedicated unit or integration tests for the pp_tps calculation or output formatting were added.

maintainer_todos.text: Run `lemonade bench <model_name>` with a downloaded model and at least one chat scenario, and confirm the table output includes a `PP t/s` column with throughput values.
Run `lemonade bench <model_name> --json` on an available local model and confirm the output includes a `pp_tps` statistics object with keys mean, min, max, p50, p95.
Run `lemonade bench <model_name> --compare <previous_results.json>` and confirm the comparison table includes a `PP change` percentage column with correct deltas.

subject: add prefill tps (#3759)
summary: Adds PP t/s (prefill throughput = prompt tokens / TTFT) to the `lemonade bench` CLI command — new `PP t/s` column in table output, `pp_tps` statistics keys (mean, min, max, p50, p95) in `--json` output, and `PP change` percentage tracking in `--compare` mode.
verdict_reason: @jeremyfowers approved with a "rubber stamp" without substantive code review, and the post-approval-commits output shows GPU metrics changes and a PR #3826 commit on the same merge queue branch that were not part of the 7-file prefill TPS merge, suggesting scope management concerns.
